title: PTE Scoring: The Integrated-Skills Strategy
summary: How PTE's 10–90 AI scoring and 'one task, two skills' design should reshape what you practise.

nodes.label: Integrated tasks
nodes.note: One task feeds two skill scores

nodes.label: Partial credit
nodes.note: Most tasks award marks per correct element

chunks.heading: The 10–90 Global Scale of English
chunks.body: PTE reports an **overall score and four skill scores (Listening, Reading, Speaking, Writing) on a 10–90 scale**, aligned to the Global Scale of English. Universities and visa authorities set their own required scores, so **check your target's exact requirement** rather than assuming a number.
chunks.realExample: A programme asking for 'PTE 65' wants an overall 65; some also set a minimum per skill (e.g. no skill below 58). Always read both the overall AND the per-skill minimums.
chunks.memoryHook: Overall + four skills, all 10–90. Check the per-skill minimum too, not just overall.

chunks.heading: Integrated tasks change what's worth practising
chunks.body: Because many tasks score **two skills at once**, the smartest prep targets the **double-scoring tasks**: Read Aloud (speaking+reading), Repeat Sentence (listening+speaking), Write from Dictation and Summarize Spoken Text (listening+writing), Summarize Written Text (reading+writing).
chunks.realExample: If your Writing is weakest, you don't only practise essays — you drill Write from Dictation and Summarize Spoken Text, because those Listening tasks also lift your Writing score.
chunks.memoryHook: Weak in one skill? Train the tasks that feed it from ANOTHER section.

chunks.heading: Enabling skills and partial credit
chunks.body: Beneath the four skills, the AI scores **'enabling skills'** — grammar, oral fluency, pronunciation, spelling, vocabulary — that cut across tasks. And most tasks give **partial credit**: you earn marks for each correct word, box or option, so **attempt everything**; a partial answer beats a blank.
chunks.realExample: A half-correct Reorder Paragraph still scores the pairs you got adjacent; a half-typed dictation still scores the right words. Never leave an item empty.
chunks.memoryHook: Partial credit everywhere — always attempt. Clean grammar & spelling lift every task.

chunks.heading: Play to the machine
chunks.body: AI scoring is **consistent and literal**: it rewards **clear pronunciation, steady fluency, correct grammar and staying within word/format limits** — and it won't be charmed by risky, complex answers that misfire. **Simple, correct and on-time wins.**
chunks.realExample: A calm, clearly-pronounced Read Aloud with no restarts outscores a faster, expressive read that stumbles — the AI is measuring intelligibility, not personality.
chunks.memoryHook: Write for the machine: clear, correct, in-range, on-time. No heroics.

recall.q: What does PTE Academic report, and on what scale?
recall.a: An overall score plus four skill scores (Listening, Reading, Speaking, Writing) on the 10–90 Global Scale of English.

recall.q: Why should a weak skill be trained through other sections' tasks?
recall.a: Because integrated tasks score two skills at once — e.g. Listening tasks like Write from Dictation also feed the Writing score.
Cross-cutting elements the AI scores — grammar, oral fluency, pronunciation, spelling and vocabulary.

recall.q: Why should you attempt every item?
recall.a: Most PTE tasks give partial credit for each correct word, box or option, so a partial answer beats a blank.

recall.q: What kind of answers does the AI reward?
recall.a: Clear, correct, in-range and on-time responses — not risky, complex ones that may misfire.
